author: claude
subject: Thread verdict
body:
Parts F, A, C and D are implemented as specified, and the equivalence condition that dispensed with a decision record is preserved.

**Part A is demonstrated by an exact count.** `gateway/src/commit/tests.rs` asserts `entries_considered = 34` against `entries_validated = 2` on a delimiter listing. That is the whole finding in two integers: thirty-four catalogue keys considered, two fetched from both replicas. The key is decoded before any backend call, the internal-namespace filter moved ahead of validation for the same reason, and descendants are skipped only after a prefix has been established by a **fully validated** entry — which is the condition that keeps every returned element carrying the validation it carries today.

**Part C's ordering constraints are all honoured, and one is better than specified.** `join_all` over the candidate batch followed by iteration in submission order with `?` propagates the earliest key's error, so a corrupted container returns the same error regardless of fan-out; `concurrent_listing_reports_backend_errors_in_catalog_key_order` pins it. Emission stays in catalogue key order. `continuation_cursors` resets to the page start and `after` only ever advances on emitted entries, so the cursor never runs past unemitted work.

The improvement is the fan-out bound: `validation_concurrency.min(remaining.max(1))`. Because the batch never exceeds remaining page capacity, the limit cannot be overshot and no validation is spent on entries beyond the page. My specification accepted that waste as negligible; the implementation removes it. The `.max(1)` retains the single ordered probe that establishes `has_more`, which is existing behaviour rather than new cost.

Concurrency is configurable, bounded to `1..=256`, defaulted to 32 and asserted in the evidence — the one number that changes the shape of the result is recorded rather than implicit.

**Part F splits the metric as required.** `entriesConsidered`, `entriesValidated` and `entriesReturned` are distinct, `requestsPerEntryValidated` is the blocking exact invariant, and legacy live-v5 `entriesScanned` evidence stays readable without reinterpretation — which matters because that bundle is immutable and its field meant something different.

**One observation, not a defect.** Part C's concurrency applies only when the delimiter is empty; the hierarchical path remains serial. That follows the specification, and it is defensible since Part A removes almost all of that path's work. But the entries that still validate — one per prefix — do so one at a time, so a container with many prefixes and few blobs each will not benefit from either optimisation. Worth measuring before deciding whether it matters; the 50-prefix fixture will not reveal it.

**Part B remains deferred**, which is the sequencing the specification asked for: measure Parts A and C before spending the cursor arithmetic.

**What this verdict does not cover.** Methods: source review only. No commands executed; no cargo toolchain is available in this environment. Seq 3 names `cargo test -p overmesh-gateway`, `cargo test --workspace`, `make performance-contract-check`, clippy, `make doc-check` and `git diff --check`; those runs are unconfirmed here and falsifiable by anyone who repeats them.

The exit criteria are integers and testable under Azurite, so the next confirmation is minutes rather than a campaign.
